anchors.paper_title: A Computational Phenotype of Disrupted Moral Inference in Borderline Personality Disorder
anchors.paper_venue: Biological Psychiatry Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging
anchors.reason: The dataset concerns EEG data in First Episode Psychosis, while the paper focuses on moral inference in Borderline Personality Disorder, making them topically related but distinct.

metadata.methods_description: Resting-state EEG was recorded for 5 minutes using an Elekta Neuromag Vectorview system with a low-impedance 60-channel 10-10 system electrode cap. Clinical assessments included Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS), Scale for Assessment of Negative Symptoms (SANS), Scale for Assessment of Positive Symptoms (SAPS), Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF), Social Functioning Scale (SFS), MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery, Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence (WASI), Hollingshead Four-Factor Index of Socioeconomic Status, and medication chlorpromazine equivalency.
